court: District Court of Appeal of Florida

issues.label: Court jurisdiction and venue
issues.why: The court must have subject-matter jurisdiction and proper venue to enter a dissolution judgment.

issues.label: Residency requirements met
issues.why: Florida dissolution requires proof of statutory residency for at least one spouse.

issues.label: Valid marriage and dissolution grounds
issues.why: The court must confirm a valid marriage and that the marriage is irretrievably broken or other statutory grounds exist.

issues.label: Date of separation relevance
issues.why: The separation date affects retroactivity, support calculations, and potentially valuation/classification issues.

issues.label: Identify minor child and status
issues.why: The court must establish the child’s age, dependency, and minority to determine custody/support duration.

issues.label: Parenting plan compliance
issues.why: A compliant parenting plan must allocate time-sharing, parental responsibility, and decision-making.

issues.label: Best interests of child
issues.why: All custody/time-sharing determinations must be supported by best-interests findings.

issues.label: Ultimate decision-making authority basis
issues.why: Granting one parent ultimate authority requires statutory findings that shared responsibility is detrimental or unworkable and that the arrangement serves the child.

issues.label: Timesharing schedule details
issues.why: The judgment must specify a workable schedule and holidays/summer to avoid ambiguity and enforcement issues.

issues.label: Health insurance for child
issues.why: The court must allocate responsibility for the child’s health insurance if reasonably available.

issues.label: Uncovered medical expense allocation
issues.why: The court must address how noncovered medical/dental/vision expenses are shared and reimbursed.

issues.label: HSA treatment and credits
issues.why: The court must determine whether HSA contributions/withdrawals are support-related, marital, and whether credits or reimbursements apply.

issues.label: Extracurricular expense allocation
issues.why: If extracurricular costs are awarded or credited, the court must set allocation, reasonableness, and proof requirements.

issues.label: Child support guideline calculation
issues.why: The court must compute child support under guidelines using accurate incomes, deductions, and timesharing.

issues.label: Income determination accuracy
issues.why: The court must determine each party’s gross and net income, including bonuses/variable pay and tax impacts.

issues.label: Imputation of income issue
issues.why: If either party is underemployed/voluntarily unemployed, the court must decide whether to impute income and make findings.

issues.label: Retroactive child support date
issues.why: The court must select the correct retroactivity start date (often filing/separation per statute/case law) and justify it.

issues.label: Credits for temporary support paid
issues.why: The court must credit the obligor for amounts paid under temporary orders or voluntarily to avoid double payment.

issues.label: Arrears calculation correctness
issues.why: Any arrears or overage must be mathematically correct and supported by evidence.

issues.label: Deviation from guidelines
issues.why: If support differs from guideline amount, the court must make required written deviation findings.

issues.label: Duration of child support
issues.why: The court must specify termination at majority and address statutory extensions (e.g., high school, disability) if applicable.

issues.label: Tax dependency exemptions
issues.why: The court should allocate the child-related tax benefits and ensure consistency with support and IRS rules.

issues.label: Allocation of child-related tax credits
issues.why: The court must decide who claims credits (CTC, childcare) and condition them on support compliance if ordered.

issues.label: Allocation of 2021 joint tax payment
issues.why: The court must equitably allocate responsibility/credits for taxes paid from joint funds in 2021.

issues.label: Post-separation tax filing impacts
issues.why: Separate 2022–2023 filings affect net incomes, credits, and equitable adjustments between spouses.

issues.label: Household contribution dispute
issues.why: The court must resolve conflicting evidence about whether joint contributions covered marital expenses and whether reimbursement is due.

issues.label: Support during pre-separation cohabitation
issues.why: The court must consider whether nonpayment while still in the home created a support arrearage or equitable claim.

issues.label: Classification of marital assets
issues.why: The court must classify assets and debts as marital or nonmarital before distribution.

issues.label: Valuation date of assets
issues.why: The court must select and justify valuation dates for assets (often near filing or trial) and apply consistently.

issues.label: Equitable distribution scheme
issues.why: The court must distribute marital assets/debts equitably and make required findings supporting any unequal distribution.

issues.label: Treatment of separate bank accounts
issues.why: Maintaining separate accounts raises tracing, commingling, and classification issues for funds and balances.

issues.label: Joint account accounting
issues.why: The court must account for joint account deposits/withdrawals and any dissipation or unilateral spending.

issues.label: Dissipation or waste claims
issues.why: If either party used marital funds improperly (e.g., stopped contributions or paid personal expenses), the court must address dissipation and remedies.

issues.label: Interim employment history relevance
issues.why: The parties’ career choices and time out/part-time work affect earning capacity and alimony factors.

issues.label: Alimony type and authority
issues.why: The court must ensure the alimony award fits statutory categories and is authorized under current law.

issues.label: Durational alimony prerequisites
issues.why: Durational alimony requires findings of need and ability to pay and is limited by statutory caps.

issues.label: Lump-sum alimony justification
issues.why: Lump-sum alimony must be supported by a permissible purpose (support or equitable distribution) and evidence of ability to pay.

issues.label: Alimony amount calculation
issues.why: The court must calculate an amount supported by need, ability to pay, and statutory factors.

issues.label: Alimony duration calculation
issues.why: The court must set duration consistent with marriage length and statutory limits and explain it.

issues.label: Alimony tax consequences
issues.why: The court should consider post-2018 federal tax treatment (generally non-deductible/non-includible) when setting amounts.

issues.label: Interrelation of alimony and distribution
issues.why: Equitable distribution and alimony must be considered together to avoid double counting or unfairness.

issues.label: Standard of living evidence
issues.why: The court must assess marital standard of living to evaluate need and reasonable expenses.

issues.label: Reasonableness of claimed expenses
issues.why: The court must determine which expenses are reasonable/necessary when calculating need and support.

issues.label: Ability to pay determination
issues.why: The court must evaluate the obligor’s net income, obligations, and available resources to pay support/alimony.

issues.label: Consideration of child-related expenses
issues.why: Child costs allocated outside guidelines affect parties’ budgets and may impact alimony need/ability.

issues.label: Health insurance/HSA for spouse
issues.why: If spousal health coverage or HSA benefits are implicated, the court must decide allocation and whether it’s support or distribution.

issues.label: Effective date of alimony
issues.why: The court must set when alimony begins and whether it is retroactive, with any credits/arrears.

issues.label: Security for support obligations
issues.why: The court should consider whether to require life insurance or other security to protect support payments.

issues.label: Attorney’s fees entitlement
issues.why: The court must address whether one party should contribute to fees based on need, ability to pay, and equitable factors.

issues.label: Costs and expert fees allocation
issues.why: Allocation of taxable costs and litigation expenses must be decided if requested and supported.

issues.label: Parent communication provisions
issues.why: The parenting plan may need provisions for communication, exchanges, and dispute resolution to be enforceable.

issues.label: Relocation considerations
issues.why: If either parent may relocate (e.g., international history), the court must ensure compliance with relocation statutes if raised.

issues.label: Contempt/enforcement history impact
issues.why: Temporary order compliance (e.g., overage/arrears) can affect credibility, credits, and enforcement provisions.

issues.label: Required written findings
issues.why: Florida family judgments often require specific written findings (income, guidelines, deviations, alimony factors) to support appellate review.

issues.label: Mathematical and clerical accuracy
issues.why: The court must ensure all calculations (support, arrears, credits) are internally consistent and correct.

issues.label: Preservation for appellate review
issues.why: Failure to move for rehearing may limit challenges to factual findings and sufficiency of evidence on appeal.

issues.label: Standard of review implications
issues.why: The appellate posture (abuse of discretion vs. competent substantial evidence) affects which issues are reviewable and how.

issues.label: Scope of relief requested in pleadings
issues.why: The court must ensure awards (alimony type, decision-making authority, retroactivity) are within the relief sought or tried by consent.

issues.label: Due process and notice
issues.why: Each party must have notice and an opportunity to be heard on disputed financial and parenting issues.
